identity.note: One character across WWFL and N.E.W., a probable: the unusual full name and the moniker on both sides (WWFL's 11 February 1998 card introduces 'ASSAF "THE TERMINATOR" LEVAVY', from Israel; N.E.W.'s King of the Mat 2, 6 April 1998, bills champion 'Assaf "The Terminator" Levavy'), the same months of 1998, and the same origin: N.E.W.'s own commentary places him from Israel ('sent back to Israel', Friday Night Slam Dance, 24 April 1998; 'back in Israel', an N.E.W. roleplay of 1999). The San Antonio, Texas billing on both N.E.W. cards is James Pillow's. The RSPWF Top 200 of 1997 also tags Assaf "The Terminator" Levavy with NEW. No document names both WWFL and N.E.W.

notes: One character with assaf-the-terminator-levavy-rspwf, the RSPWF Top 200 entry: the poll bills the same 'Assaf "The Terminator" Levavy', tags him NEW, the N.E.W. of this record's 1998 tenure, and its 1997 entry (#139) carries his prior-year place '#40', the 1996 list's 'Assaf "The Terminator'" Levavy'. Presumed one character with the two 1998 RSPWF poll entries, 'Assa Levavy' (Top 300 Wrestlers, #245) and '"The Terminator" Asaaf Levavy' (Worst 200 Gimmicks, #57): the same unusual surname, the moniker and the Asaaf spelling (also used on APCW's and WCWF's cards), in the same newsgroup's polls of the year of his WWFL and N.E.W. runs. The wider record agrees on one wrestler from 1996 to 2002: 300 lbs from Israel on APCW (1996), 6' 3" and 300 pounds on UWA (1997) as on WWFL (1998); Patty Babes Carter's BWA biography (September 1997) has the two found the Renaissance Movement in January 1997, which SJPW's Ring Wars (June 1997) also names; N.E.W.'s King of the Mat 2 (1998) bills Carter, his 'former friend', as his title challenger; NIWF LEGENDS (2001) headlines the two again.
